Floor One · Gallery, baithak room, classroom, stage

A creative, conscious community one floor above the noise of JVPD. Exhibitions, modern baithaks, painting classes and the occasional play.

Armaan, 23 Hatkesh Society · NS Road 6 See what’s on →
About the floor( @floorone.juhu )

Floor One is a gallery that doubles as a living room — a place in Juhu for people who would rather spend an evening with a painter, a khayal singer or a brush in their own hand than on a screen.

Independent and artist-run, one floor above NS Road 6. Four programmes, one room, a community that turns up.

Choose your door.

Come to look, come to listen, come to make something, or come to sit with sixty strangers who will not be strangers by the interval.

( 01 )

Exhibitions

Group shows, solos, fundraisers

White walls, warm light and an opening night that spills on to the stairs. Recent shows have ranged from a fifteen-artist porcelain-and-painting collective to a solo of marbled canvases that went on to the India Art Festival.

Best for
  • Collectors who like to meet the artist
  • First-time buyers
  • Anyone with a free Sunday afternoon
What to expect
  • Shows run three days to three weeks
  • Most are open 11am–7pm
  • Prices on request, framed and ready
See the current show →
( 02 )

Baithaks

Modern baithaks for curious souls

Māhaul brings Hindustani classical back to the floor it was written for. Timeless bandishes, ghazals and the odd khayal, sung from a mattress six feet away rather than a stage sixty feet away. Baithak #5, “Raagas & Beyond”, filled the room in September.

Best for
  • Listeners who want to hear the breath
  • Beginners, with a host who explains the raag
  • Saturdays, 6pm onwards
What to expect
  • Floor seating, chairs at the back
  • Chai at the interval
  • Tickets by DM, limited to the room
DM “ticket” for the next one →
( 03 )

Classes & workshops

With A Class Apahrt

Weekly painting and hand-painted porcelain sessions run by A Class Apahrt, whose students hung their own show, “Showtime”, on these walls this October. No prior training; the brushes are supplied, the patience is yours.

Best for
  • Adults who stopped drawing at twelve
  • Small groups and the occasional birthday
  • Anyone who wants a show of their own one day
What to expect
  • Two to three hours, materials included
  • Six to ten people per table
  • Your piece goes home with you
Ask about the next batch →
( 04 )

Stage & gatherings

Theatre, talks, kindness projects

The same floor clears for a Neoyug play, a poetry evening or an art fundraiser. “The Kindness Project”, with Burgundy Art Gallery, raised money for YODA and made the mid-day guide page. The room is small enough that nobody is in the back row.

Best for
  • Intimate theatre and readings
  • Launches that want a gallery, not a banquet hall
  • Causes that need a room and a crowd
What to expect
  • Seating for roughly sixty
  • Sound and warm lighting in-house
  • Walls stay art; the floor adapts

Before you comeFive questions

Good to know.

When are you open?

Floor One opens around its programme rather than a shop timetable. Exhibitions usually run 11am to 7pm daily; baithaks and plays are evenings, 6pm onwards. The current list is on this page under “On the floor”, and Instagram is updated the same day anything changes.

Is there an entry fee?

Exhibitions are free to walk into. Baithaks, workshops and plays are ticketed because the room is small; tickets go by DM and are limited to the seats on the floor.

Where exactly is the first floor?

Armaan, 23 Hatkesh Society, NS Road 6, JVPD Scheme, Juhu, Mumbai 400056. Take the stairs past the building lobby; the door with the square logo is ours. Street parking on NS Road 6 is easier before 6pm.

Can I buy what is on the wall?

Almost always. Ask at the desk or message the handle on the placard. Framed works go home with you after the show closes; we can arrange delivery within Mumbai.

Can I hold a private event here?

If it has art, music, words or making at its centre, yes. Birthday painting sessions, book readings, small launches and fundraisers have all happened here. Send a note with the date and the idea.
